subject: Configurable lifecycle + regional storage: admin API / UI requirements
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Configurable lifecycle + regional storage: admin API / UI requirements

Hi Julia / NovaPayments security team,

Thanks for the questionnaire — attached are the high-level retention asks you shared and a small summary of gaps we need to resolve on our side. To make sure we land on an implementation that meets your compliance needs without blocking rollout, I want to align internal product + infra workstreams. Key asks from NovaPayments (from the attached spreadsheet):

- Per-tenant retention TTL that can be configured by the admin (granularity: days/weeks/months)
- Option to pin tenant data to a US-only region (data-at-rest locality) with explicit routing guarantees
- Ability to perform legal-hold / preservation for specific accounts for a configurable window

High-level questions for engineering/product:
1) Surface: do we need an admin API only, or must we expose these controls in Console UI for customers to self-serve?
2) Policy semantics: do we support both absolute deletion (hard delete) and soft-delete + purge windows?
3) Operational guardrails: what guardrails do we need to prevent accidental tenant-wide hard-deletes (approval workflow / two-step)?

Grace / Lauren — can you weigh in on feasibility and rough effort (RFC + implementation) so I can share an ETA with NovaPayments next week? Julia — attaching their security questionnaire and the spreadsheet for transparency: [Attachment: NovaPayments_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: retention_requirements.xlsx (XLSX)].

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Configurable lifecycle + regional storage: admin API / UI requirements

Karthik / Lauren,

Quick technical readout after scanning the questionnaire and the requirements sheet: we can deliver the core capabilities but there are trade-offs and one blocker that needs product decisions. Summary below.

1) Storage locality (US-only pinning)
- We already have region tags on tenant metadata and routing policies in Smart Router, which can pin requests to US-hosted placements.
- Gap: object lifecycle and cold storage replication settings are currently set at placement level; we would need per-tenant placement overrides to guarantee no cross-region replication. Effort: small-medium (2–3 sprint effort across placement manager + scheduler).

2) Per-tenant TTLs and retention policy semantics
- Implementing TTL as metadata on tenant config is straightforward; the complexity is in deleting cached KV + prefix caches across the serving fleet and ensuring deletion jobs are propogated and idempotent.
- Soft-delete + purge window is safer and aligns with our backups/restore model; hard-delete must also remove backups (requires retention metadata in backup service). Effort: 3–4 sprints for safe soft-delete workflow + admin API; additional 1–2 sprints for hard-delete purge that removes backups.

3) Legal hold / preservation flags
- We can add a per-tenant / per-entity legal_hold boolean that overrides TTL and blocks purge. This requires changes in the purge pipeline and a small UI/CLI workflow for triage. Effort: 1–2 sprints.

4) Approval & guardrails
- Propose: destructive actions (hard-delete, override legal hold) require a two-step approval via Console: (i) request with rationale stored in Audit Log, (ii) 24-hour delay window, (iii) execution only after explicit confirm. We should also provide an API that returns a signed audit token for compliance evidence.

Blocker: backup lifecycle metadata is currently global per-placement. To fully guarantee no cross-region snapshot retention for pinned tenants, we need backup service changes. That is the critical path for NovaPayments' US-only requirement.

Next steps I recommend:
- Product to finalize semantics (soft-delete vs hard-delete, default purge windows, legal_hold policy model).
- Engineering to open RFC covering: API shape, Console flows, purge pipeline changes, backup service migration plan, and rollout strategy (canary on non-critical tenants first).

I can draft the RFC if product confirms the design choices — estimate 5 working days for a first draft.

-Grace
Senior Infra Engineer
Grace O'Connor | redwood.ai

[Attachment: design_sketch_placement_override.png (PNG) referenced in body]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@novapayments.com>, security@novapayments.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Configurable lifecycle + regional storage: admin API / UI requirements

Thanks Grace — this is actionable. A few product decisions to confirm so RFC can shape correctly:

1) Default behavior: tenants without an explicit retention policy should inherit the account-level default of 90 days (soft-delete -> purge after 30 days). Does engineering agree this is implementable without extra infra changes?
2) Policy model: expose three policy types in the admin API: "default", "custom-ttl", "legal-hold". "custom-ttl" accepts ISO duration and a purge-mode enum (soft|hard).
3) Console UX: admin can set region pinning at onboarding or change later, but changing region pinning must trigger an automated impact checklist and cannot be used to bypass an existing legal hold.
4) Audit trail: every change to retention/region pinning must emit an immutable audit event with operator, timestamp, and reason. We want to attach audit_id in the API response for each mutation so customers can reference it in their compliance systems.

Assuming the above, please proceed with RFC. Grace — can you include the backup-service migration plan as a separate section; call out required downtime (if any), migration timeline, and rollback strategy.

Julia / NovaPayments — this design would let you self-serve retention and region pinning from Console or via API. We will surface the audit_id in the UI and include the approval workflow for destructive actions. Would you prefer that we ship admin-API-only first and Console in phase 2?

Action items / owners:
- Grace: RFC draft + backup migration plan (ETA: 5 business days)
- Karthik: share ETA with NovaPayments after RFC draft
- Lauren: mockups for Console admin flows (ETA: 7 business days)

Thanks,
Lauren
Product Manager — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@novapayments.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@novapayments.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Configurable lifecycle + regional storage: admin API / UI requirements

Hi Lauren / Karthik / Grace,

Thanks for the quick read and constructive plan. NovaPayments prefers the following approach:
- Phase 1: Admin API + audit_id surfaced in API responses. We want programmatic controls integrated into our internal compliance tooling first.
- Phase 2: Console self-serve for non-destructive changes (custom-ttl, view audit events).
- Phase 3: Console-driven destructive actions only after we validate the API flows.

For the legal hold requirement, we need a per-entity (user-account) preserve flag in addition to per-tenant. If the design supports both, we can proceed.

Also, please include a one-page compliance summary (template) that lists: region pinning guarantees, backup snapshot behavior, audit log retention, and the approval workflow for destructive actions. That will speed our internal approval.

Looking forward to the RFC. Let us know if any additional info is helpful.

Best,
Julia Nguyen
Director, Information Security — NovaPayments
security@novapayments.com
